title: Model Server Crashes Every Morning at 9am
intro: The recommendation model server restarts several times every weekday around 9am, then is fine the rest of the day. Users see empty recommendation widgets during those minutes.

steps.prompt: Check the pods' restart counts and status.
steps.fake_output:
NAME                         READY  STATUS   RESTARTS      AGE
recs-model-7d8f9c6b5-x2z9k   1/1    Running  14 (3h ago)   6d
recs-model-7d8f9c6b5-a1b2c   1/1    Running  12 (3h ago)   6d
steps.hint: Many restarts, all around the same time.

steps.prompt: Find out why the last container instance terminated.
steps.fake_output:
Last State:  Terminated
  Reason:    OOMKilled
  Exit Code: 137
Limits:
  memory: 2Gi
steps.hint: Exit code 137 means killed by SIGKILL.

steps.prompt: OOMKilled at a 2Gi limit. Check the logs from before the last crash for clues about what happens at 9am.
steps.fake_output:
INFO batch received size=32
INFO batch received size=32
INFO batch received size=512 (morning digest job)
INFO batch received size=512
steps.hint: --previous shows the logs of the container that crashed.

steps.prompt: A 9am email-digest job sends 512-item batches instead of the usual 32. Check the model server's config for a batch size cap.
steps.hint: Is there any limit on how large a batch can be?

resolution: Normal traffic sends small batches, but a scheduled morning email-digest job sends batches 16x larger. Memory needed for inference scales with batch size, and with no cap configured (MAX_BATCH_SIZE=0), those batches pushed the server past its 2Gi limit — the kernel OOM-killed it, it restarted, and got hit again. The fix: cap the server-side batch size (e.g. 64) so large client requests are split into chunks, and size the memory limit from load-testing the realistic maximum batch rather than typical traffic. Also worth separating the batch digest job onto its own model deployment (or a batch-inference pipeline), so bulk offline workloads can never take out the real-time path users see.
